title: Fix Omron FINS response code lookup when error bit is set
description:
When any of the Relay Error, PC Fatal Error, or PC Non-fatal Error bits are set in the main- and sub-code of the response code the lookup into `response_codes` will fail.

In addition to fixing the response code lookup this also adds new tree items for the error bits.

[response_codes_with_error_bits.pcapng](/uploads/abdb0ab1a216bded5a38ebaba0c2f1a0/response_codes_with_error_bits.pcapng)

can you look follwing warning :

`Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-omron-fins.c hf_omron_response_code filter= omron.response.code  - mask with non-contiguous bits 0x7F3F ( 0x7f3f )`

May be use proto_tree_add_bitmask ?
I'll take a look at this soon. Out of town this week, may not get to it until next weekend.

@alagoutte I'm not sure if `proto_tree_add_bitmask` is the right thing here - the response code value really is stored, looked up by, and referred to by the 16-bit value you get by applying this non-contiguous bit mask (`0x7F3F`).

Is there some other alternative?

> the 16-bit value you get by applying this non-contiguous bit mask (`0x7F3F`)

0x7F3F is 0b0111111100111111, which has 13 bits set.

Given that, and given that the bits are not contiguous, I don't see why proto_tree_add_bitmask()` would *not* be the right thing here.

Are the other 3 bits in that 16-bit field used for any other purpose?

> Are the other 3 bits in that 16-bit field used for any other purpose?

Yes, they are, so you have a 16-bit item that contains four bitfields - the three flags and the error code. That's what `proto_tree_add_bitmask()` was created for.

Ok I think what's confusing me is that `omron.response.code` already exists, and originally I was just trying to fix the lookup that used this value. 

To use `proto_tree_add_bitmask` I need a new "host" field for the entire 16-bit item, then `omron.response.code` gets repurposed as one of the fields calculated by applying the `0x7F3f` mask?

> To use `proto_tree_add_bitmask` I need a new "host" field for the entire 16-bit item,

No, just use `omron.response.code`, as it is, for that purpose, as [the FINS Commands Reference Manual](https://www.myomron.com/downloads/1.Manuals/Networks/W227E12_FINS_Commands_Reference_Manual.pdf) calls the full 16-bit field the "response code".

> then `omron.response.code` gets repurposed as one of the fields calculated by applying the `0x7F3f` mask?

No, you would then have five subfields of `omron.response.code` - `omron.response.code.relay_error`, `omron.response.code.mres`, `omron.response.code.fatal_error`, `omron.response.code.non_fatal_error`, and `omron.response.code.sres`.  The SRES is a bit tricky, as the interpretation of `omron.response.code.sres` depends on the value of `omron.response.code.mres`. Alternatively, you could have a single `omron.response.code.msres` field that combines the MRES and SRES.

commits_data.title: Fix response code lookup when error bit is set
commits_data.message:
Fix response code lookup when error bit is set

When any of the Relay Error, PC Fatal Error, or PC Non-fatal Error bits are set in the main- and sub-code of the response code the lookup into `response_codes` will fail.

Additionally, adds tree items for response code error bits:
- Relay Error
- PC Fatal Error
- PC Non-fatal Error
